blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a compelling idea from this OOPSLA 2015 paper: integrating runtime monitoring data from production deployments directly into developers' IDEs to create tighter feedback loops, a concept termed 'feedback-driven development' (FDD). The paper argues that operational data is often siloed in monitoring tools designed for operations teams, making it difficult for developers to act on it. The authors propose mapping this data onto source code artifacts (e.g., via abstract syntax trees) to annotate and inform development. A key insight is addressing the relevance of operational data over time, especially in continuous deployment environments, by using statistical changepoint analysis to determine when historical data is no longer applicable. The paper demonstrates the concept through three tools: Performance Spotter (IDE-integrated performance profiling), Performance Hat (Eclipse plugin for hotspot identification and loop execution time prediction), and a cost-of-changes visualizer to raise awareness of cloud application costs.
paper_title: Runtime Metric Meets Developer - Building Better Cloud Applications Using Feedback
paper_abstract: For software developers, source code is the static blueprint that is transformed into running behavior. In modern applications, this behavior is often facilitated through distributed systems. Thus, behavior developers observe on their machine is usually not the same as it is perceived by end users. We propose a system where source code is mapped with information gathered at runtime to make programs feel “alive". We implemented a system that maps runtime performance to source code artifacts.
